full_judgment:
Jahangir Hossain, J: A Division Bench of tilt High Court Division by order dated 15-12-2016 issued a Rule calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 27-9-2016 passed by the learned Special Sessions Judge, Patuakhali in Criminal Revision No. 20 of 2016 arising out of CR Case No. 443 of 2014 initiated under section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1980 setting aside the order dated 5-1-2016 passed by the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, 1st Court, Patuakhali in CR Case No. 443 of 2014 should not be quashed. 

 3. Upon receipt of the complaint, the learned Magistrate took cognizance against the accused-petitioner under section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1980. Thereafter, having appeared in the case the accused-petitioner filed an application before the trial court for discharge from the case under section 241 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was allowed upon hearing of both the parties. Against which the complainant filed Criminal Revision No. 20 of 2016 in the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Patuakhali. Ultimately, the learned Special Sessions Judge, Patuakhali allowed the revision setting aside the order of the trial court. 

 5. Mr AK Rashedul Huq, learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner contends that the complainant-opposite party files cases one after another containing false allegation against the accused-petitioner. The divorce between the accused-petitioner and the complaint-opposite parties look place long before. The accused-petitioner, meanwhile, paid all the money, claimed by the complainant-opposite party through Family Execution Case No. 1 of 2019 in Family Court, Patuakhali Sadar, Patuakhali. 

 6. As per official note dated 5-10-2017 the complainant opposite-party entered appearance in the present case through learned Advocate Mr Purnindu Bikash Das, but no one appeared for the complainant opposite-party when it was taken up for hearing. 

 8. Heard the submissions of the learned Advocates and perused the application along with materials on record wherefrom it appears that the alleged occurrence took place on 17-1-2014 at about 10-00 am but the petition of complaint was filed on 15-6-2014 after expiry of 51/2 months of the alleged occurrence. It also reveals from the judgment dated 13-11-2019 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 27493 of 2016, that the complaint-opposite party filed another criminal case being Nari-o-Shishu Case No. 604 of 2015 against the accused-petitioner under section 11(Ga) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 wherein the proceeding was quashed by the High Court Division. It has further noticed from the said judgment that the complainant subsequently filed Family Suit being No. 06 of 2016 impleading the present accused-petitioner as defendant in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Patuakhali Sadar for dower and maintenance. The said suit was decreed on 27-11-2018. In the Execution Case being No. 1 of 2019, the present accused-petitioner did not challenge the decree rather he paid the decreetal amount to the complainant opposite party who received the same by giving an acknowledgement receipt. Therefore, the judgment and decree passed in the Family Suit has reached its finality. It is also evident that the accused-petitioner had already divorced the complainant opposite-party on 26-5-2014 and the notice was duly served upon both the complainant opposite-party and the local Chairman on 2-6-2014 prior to initiating the present case. Though the marriage between the parties ended in divorce on 26-8-2014 but the overall fact remains that the marriage between the parties is no longer subsisting. In the present case, it is found that the claim for dowry by the accused-petitioner was made long after the divorce. Therefore, the claim for dowry in the present case does not come within the mischief of the definition of dowry as laid down in section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1980. It reveals from record that the complainant opposite-party lodges complaint containing the proceeding one after another that can be said to be an abuse of the process of the court. 

 9. For the forging reasons, the impugned judgment and order dated 27-9-2016 passed by the learned Special Sessions Judge, Patuakhali is illegal and the continuance of proceedings of the present case is, hereby, quashed.
